extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. The benchmark comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark evaluates 21 open-source models and GPT-4o-Audio, measuring the quality of response content, speech, and consistency.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.citeAs: VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. For role-play tasks, texts from RoleBench were utilized, and 100 distinct roles were selected with three representative audio clips per role. Speech instructions were synthesized using three advanced TTS models (F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B), evaluated with UTMOS, and regenerated if scores were below 3.8. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper and compared to original instructions, retaining only the lowest word error rate samples. A multi-stage curation process included deduplication (lexical overlap and edit-distance matching), filtering incomplete or inappropriate items (~10% removed), mapping to 13 task categories, and balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web API, Experiments, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source datasets included MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, SpeechInstructBench, Clotho, SLURP, Clotho-AQA, CoVOST2, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, MELD, GSM8K, STORAL, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, MyST, LibriSpeech, Clotho, AudioCaps, A VQA, MusicCaps, MUSIA-A VQA, SUPERB, HEAR, AIR-Bench, MMMU, MathVista, MATH-Vision.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing steps included: 1) Text rewriting using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to ensure accurate TTS synthesis (e.g., converting 'OC= 2rsin(π)' to 'O C equals two r times sine of pi' and '$31,000' to 'thirty-one thousand dollars'). 2) Rephrasing multiple-choice options for better readability. 3) Using UTMOS Strong to evaluate synthesized speech and regenerating until scores surpassed 3.8. 4) Transcribing synthesized audio with Whisper-Large-v3 and selecting samples with the lowest word error rate. 5) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, followed by manual review. 6) Filtering incomplete or inappropriate items (e.g., corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, incorrect answers), removing ~10% of candidates. 7) Mapping remaining problems to 13 predefined task categories and applying balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created through a multi-stage process: 1) For role-play tasks, role-specific speaking style and vocal timbre were analyzed using texts from RoleBench. 2) Annotations for listening, speaking, and viewing tasks were generated by evaluating model responses across three dimensions: content quality (using gpt-oss-20b), speech quality (using UTMOS), and consistency between text and speech modalities (using Whisper-Large-v3 transcription and modified Word Error Rate). 3) For role-play tasks, speaker similarity was calculated using Wespeaker. 4) Human evaluation was conducted on 10% of model responses to validate automated scoring, achieving high agreement rates (96.1%) and Pearson correlation coefficients (0.73–1.00).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI et al., 2025) for content quality evaluation, UTMOS (Saeki et al., 2022) for speech quality, Whisper-Large-v3 (Radford et al., 2022) for transcription and consistency evaluation, Wespeaker (Wang et al., 2023b; 2024c) for speaker similarity in role-play tasks, emotion2vec (Ma et al., 2023) for emotion analysis.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validated the automated scoring scheme, showing high agreement rates (96.1%) and Pearson correlation coefficients (0.73–1.00) between automated and human judgments across tasks. Error analysis revealed specific difficulties: listening tasks were hindered by context loss (46%) and perception errors (speech 16%, sound 15%); speaking tasks showed insufficient answers (25%) and requirement deviations (23%); viewing tasks were dominated by vision perception errors (50%).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code will be publicly released under an MIT license. Versioning will follow community contributions and updates, with deprecation policies to be determined based on model advancements and ethical considerations. Maintenance will include auditing for consent and licensing issues, and updates to address identified biases or safety concerns.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes role-play voice imitation tasks that may involve personalization aspects, but no explicit sensitive human attributes (e.g., gender, socio-economic status, geography, language, age, culture, experience) are collected as part of the dataset. The role-play tasks use predefined roles and audio clips, but these are not tied to real individuals.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to push the boundaries of AI assistant capabilities across listening, speaking, and viewing, addressing gaps in existing benchmarks such as lack of voice personalization evaluation, limited focus on hands-free interaction, neglect of diverse audio contexts, and insufficient multi-modal integration assessment. The benchmark identifies challenges in multimodal (audio plus visual) input, role-play voice imitation, robustness, and safety alignment, highlighting the need for improved models in these areas.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases from its source data and design choices, such as the use of academic or synthetic sources and predefined roles in role-play tasks. The roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The benchmark encourages community analysis of model outputs for biases or unsafe behavior and contributions of additional test cases to probe fairness and ethical considerations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: 1) Monolingual focus (English) may not capture global usage diversity. 2) Limited model evaluation scope (primarily open-source models, with only one proprietary model included). 3) Evaluation methodology relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias. 4) Biases from source data and design choices may affect fairness and realism. 5) Gaps in task coverage and scenario realism, such as lack of video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks. 6) Offline, static evaluation may not capture real-world deployment factors like latency constraints and incremental speech processing.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The benchmark is intended for researchers and practitioners to evaluate the listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities of AI assistants, facilitating the development of more capable, fair, and versatile multimodal AI systems. Usage guidelines emphasize responsible use, including consent gating and watermarking for synthetic audio, and prohibiting training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent.
